contentHtml:
Los Comales Waterfall (Cascada Los Comales) is a waterfall tucked into the humid mountains of Xilitla, San Luis Potosí, with a local fee of ~$20 MXN per person and no need to hire a guide. Many travelers come to Xilitla thinking only about Edward James's Surrealist Garden and miss the fact that, just meters away, Los Comales Waterfall and other water features are waiting with far fewer crowds. The real question isn't whether to go, but knowing which ones to visit and how to fit them into a single day without wasting time.

This article brings together the lesser-known waterfalls near Xilitla that complement—or even top—the castle experience. You'll find updated prices, travel times and nature travel tips to make the most of every hour. According to local operators in the Huasteca Potosina, more and more visitors combine Las Pozas with at least one more waterfall, which confirms that travelers are looking for more than architecture.

At huasteca-potosina.com we work with local guides and operators across the region. This guide is updated with the real experiences of people who travel the Huasteca Potosina every week. Last updated: September 2026. Before you set out, book your guided tour in the Huasteca Potosina to make the most of your stay in the Potosí mountains.

What to see in Xilitla beyond the castle: the waterfalls nobody tells you about

Los Comales Waterfall: the falls across from Edward James's garden

Los Comales Waterfall is about 50 meters from the entrance to the famous Surrealist Garden, although access is completely separate. Admission is a local fee of ~$20 MXN per person, and it's a daytime visit; it's closed on Tuesdays (like Las Pozas). Prices and hours aren't officially published: confirm by phone.

Travelers usually spend 45 to 90 minutes here before continuing on to Las Pozas, which makes it easy to combine both in a single morning. Book a tour to Xilitla if you'd rather arrive with transportation included from Ciudad Valles.

Los Tepales natural pools: crystal-clear water 15 minutes from Xilitla

Just 15 minutes by car from downtown Xilitla, Los Tepales has a chain of pools that step down between moss-covered rocks. The best time to visit is between June and October, when the water flow is at its peak; wear shoes with a firm grip.

If you want to understand the area's natural and cultural context before you go, read about the history and myths of Xilitla to arrive with more background on the Huasteca mountains.

Prices, access and what to expect on Xilitla waterfall tours in 2026

How do you get to Los Comales Waterfall from Ciudad Valles?

It's an hour and a half drive to Xilitla, taking Federal Highway 85 and turning off onto Federal Highway 120. Once in Xilitla, the garden's entrance is your starting point (the road has no parking lot). The route fills up over the November long weekend, so arriving before 9:00 a.m. makes all the difference. See available tours in the Huasteca Potosina departing from Ciudad Valles.

How much does it cost to visit Los Comales Waterfall and the nearby falls?

Admission to Los Comales Waterfall is a local fee of ~$20 MXN per person, paid at the entrance with no reservation needed. If you combine it with Edward James's Surrealist Garden, add the garden's admission, $180 MXN per adult. To plan your full budget, our article on how much it costs to visit the Huasteca Potosina in 2026 has a detailed breakdown by type of traveler.

Tips before visiting Los Comales and the waterfalls of Xilitla

  • Get there early: The entrance opens at 8:00 a.m.; on weekdays and before 10:00 a.m., crowds are light and the light for photos is the best of the day.
  • Wear shoes with grip: The rocks stay wet; flip-flops aren't a good idea. Check the packing checklist for the Potosí jungle before you pack.
  • Check the weather: The best time to visit Xilitla is between November and April, when rain is less frequent.
  • Bring cash: The ticket booth only takes cash; withdraw money in Ciudad Valles before you leave.

Frequently asked questions about Los Comales Waterfall

Can you swim at Los Comales Waterfall?

Yes: Los Comales Waterfall forms pools of lukewarm water that are fine for swimming. Wear non-slip shoes, because the rocks are slippery.

How much is admission to Los Comales Waterfall in 2026?

Admission is a local fee of ~$20 MXN per person, paid at the entrance. It's separate from the ticket for Edward James's Surrealist Garden. No reservation needed; it's a daytime visit, and it's closed on Tuesdays (like Las Pozas).

How do you get to Los Comales Waterfall from Ciudad Valles?

Take Federal Highway 85 to the turnoff onto Federal Highway 120, a drive of about an hour and a half. There's public transportation from downtown Xilitla, although it doesn't run often.

Is Los Comales Waterfall good for families with kids?

Yes. The trail is accessible and easy, a good fit for nature outings with the family. Wear closed-toe shoes with good grip and bring enough water. For more family activities, see what to see in Xilitla with kids in 2026.
